source_checks.note: 2026-10-18 (stage-deciding document, reviewer read on govinfo.gov): introduced text of H.R.9329. Sec. 301 (Title III, SEC Cybersecurity) requires the Comptroller General, within one year of enactment, to audit SEC IT infrastructure and data handling, covering (A) SEC IT spending compared with other federal financial regulators, (B) the quality and effectiveness of SEC IT contracting, (C) data and cybersecurity systems and (D) recent IT incidents, with a report to the SEC and the House and Senate committees. This matches the GAO report element of the recommendation. No time limit on SEC investigations appears anywhere: the 'two years' references are PCAOB transfer provisions in Title V (Secs. 501(d), 509, 511), and Sec. 801 concerns counting violations. No inspector general role. Partial match to the recommendation as a whole.

2026-10-18 (reviewer read for check 3): BILLSTATUS shows introduction 2026-06-18 (sponsor a Republican member from Missouri), referral to Financial Services, markup and order to report as amended by yeas and nays 28 to 23 on 2026-06-30, and no later action. status_summary: H.R.9329, the SEC Reform and Restructuring Act, was introduced on 2026-06-18, and the House Financial Services Committee ordered it reported as amended by 28 to 23 on 2026-06-30. In the introduced text, Sec. 301 directs the Comptroller General to audit SEC information technology within one year of enactment, including a comparison of SEC IT spending with other federal financial regulators and the quality and effectiveness of SEC IT contracting, which matches the report element of the recommendation. No provision limiting SEC investigations to two years was found in that text or in any other bill, and the SEC Office of Inspector General's report list through 2026-09-28 shows no IT spending and contracting review. At a 2025-05-06 town hall the SEC Chairman mentioned an internal review of technology infrastructure and contracts, which is not the statutory step the Mandate asks Congress to take.

timeline.event: H.R.9329, the SEC Reform and Restructuring Act, is introduced in the House and referred to the Committee on Financial Services; Sec. 301 of the introduced text directs a Comptroller General audit of SEC information technology, including a comparison of SEC IT spending with other federal financial regulators and the quality of SEC IT contracting. The text sets no time limit on SEC investigations.

The House Committee on Financial Services holds a markup and orders H.R.9329 reported, as amended, by a recorded vote of 28 to 23; no reported text, report number or floor action appears in the bill status record.
